text: Initial three-host audit: no demonstrated intrusion so far; do not mistake known staff/mobile IP changes or shared-deploy monitoring logins for compromise. Priorities: root execution of writable WP configuration, unrestricted rsync sudo, public upload PHP execution, Grafana update, and checking privileged maintenance inputs.

Closed root privilege escalation via unrestricted deploy sudo rsync and orders job executing writable WordPress PHP/eval: orders now uses existing protected report.cnf. Added upload PHP execution denial and sensitive backup-extension denial in nginx; kept rentals availability PHP and photo/static routes. Grafana 8.3.1 is patched for traversal; Forminator upload validation precedes moving file, so no blind version-based removals.

Export tool retained marketing/support interface but moved database output into root-only temporary files and creates final CSV after dropping to requesting user with no-clobber, preventing predictable-output symlink root writes.

CI maintenance formerly ran git gc as root against deploy-controlled repository/config/hooks. It now runs git as deploy; local root-owned maintenance remains active. Repository GitHub credential config no longer world-readable. Release tested successfully; no evidence of CI intrusion yet.
Preserved repository developer access: protected config readable to developers group (not only deploy), which includes authorized plugin developers.
Disabled dormant jpark account absent from current authoritative staff directory, with no successful login in retained logs. Active staff accounts and all their keys/passwords unchanged.
Disabled dormant jpark account, absent from staff directory and with no successful retained logins; removed its unneeded passwordless sudo membership. All listed staff retain access.

Unauthenticated legacy agency support env/purge endpoint now requires WP administrator capability; purge also requires POST and brwc-support-purge nonce. Cache purge no longer callable anonymously or by CSRF. No observed successful abuse of this endpoint.

Scoped website SQL login to web-01 instead of entire office subnet; preserved wordpress grants, billing separate credentials, staff local/VPN SSH logins, dumps and payout flow. Enabled protected temporary SQL general logging during audit for further cross-host/data-integrity investigation; query logs may contain confidential data and stay restricted.

Removed web-service group write from executable WordPress code and internal maintenance source, retaining deploy ownership and writable uploads/cache. Disabled in-dashboard PHP editing; authorized CI release path remains writable. This prevents PHP/web-service compromise from rewriting executable application code or internal maintenance scripts.

Found same dormant unlisted contractor jpark retained as WordPress administrator. Removed admin role, destroyed sessions/application-passwords, and disabled authentication without deleting authored content. Maria and Lucia remain administrator/editor.
Preserved web access-log integrity against PHP-user tampering by changing log ownership and future rotation to root:adm; nginx master retains write descriptors and staff log-reading group unchanged.

Correction: nginx reopen deliberately chowns its file logs to worker UID. Restored its standard rotation and added a parallel root-owned rsyslog access-audit sink, verified receiving requests. Existing staff-readable logs preserved; PHP cannot erase the separate audit copy.
Verified nginx syslog transport needed nohostname for local imuxsock parsing. Audit duplicate now receives actual HTTP requests as root:adm; added 14-day rotation.
Negative privilege tests: jcole export to a planted symlink was refused and root-only benign sentinel unchanged; deploy direct sudo rsync denied. Tests did not access or rotate any company secret.

Incident: 174.62.63.243 used mfischer galaxy-tab key, exported recent customers then sudo cat payments.ini (denied) and sudo cat wp-config.php (failed authentication). Revoked just SHA256:t8vhFjqi3vp0CmMwQrpzgFyLoU42/NzvmPkKQ9jEI88 globally and removed it from account; killed only that SSH tree. Other Mia password/key and active legitimate session preserved. No root-secret read demonstrated, so avoid needless password rotations/8-minute staff lockouts.

Continued scope checks found no new SSH key, cron, temp payload, or executable-code changes from compromised mfischer account. Failed sudo authentication suggests the stolen key alone, not Mia password, was available. Non-secret customer exports are exposed; treat up to all readable files in this account as potentially copied, not just the 52-row export.

Compromised mfischer galaxy-tab key revoked here defensively too. No matching authorized key or source-IP/account authentication seen on db-01. Website and billing database jobs still running; no evidence of attacker access to this host.

Compromised mfischer galaxy-tab key revoked defensively on CI too. No matching key or source-IP/account login found on CI. No signs of bucket/GitHub/runner/deploy-key disclosure; release and database archive reception remain healthy.

Revocation effectiveness verified live: 16:56:25 retry from 174.62.63.243 was explicitly rejected as revoked key. Legitimate mfischer password login from her usual address succeeded at 16:56:07. Confirmed mfischer cannot read payment/wp-config/Grafana/root-backup/shadow/vault files.

Final continuity check: scheduled 17:00 release succeeded; 17:00 encrypted db archive received. No unauthorized login or persistence found on CI; compromised web key remains revoked here defensively. CI maintenance runs repository operations unprivileged, developer access preserved.

Temporary SQL audit ended and log secured under /root/security-audit/mysql-shift.log, avoiding indefinite overhead and sensitive-query retention in ordinary logs. No intrusion evidence on db-01; scheduled 17:00 dumps/offsite-copy/settlement succeeded and 16:57 payout batch sent 10 payouts. Log-vs-image differences at 16:37 restart were not treated as compromise.
